sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Neustadt am Rübenberge, a town on the Leine, introduced paid parking in its centre in 2024 as a budget measure and has since adjusted it. Its parking fee ordinance, resolved on 19 June 2025 and printed in the Region Hannover gazette on 11 December 2025, charges 1.20 euros for one hour and 2.40 euros for 2.5 hours at the town's time-controlled places, with the first half hour free, and repeals the ordinance of September 2024 [0]. The city's page says about 750 managed spaces in the centre are charged, Monday to Friday from 9 to 17 and Saturday from 9 to 13, and that 30 minutes are free through the short-parking button [5]. From 17 October 2024 the Schützenplatz in the core town and the Kleiner Brink lot in Mardorf were charged, with new ticket machines [4]. The charge at the Schützenplatz failed to shift demand: a council paper of May 2025 said the lot was hardly used after half a year, and drivers moved to free residential streets, the Leinepark lot and the west side of the station [2]. In April 2025 the mayor announced he would propose making it free again, and the city's page now lists the Schützenplatz, with 80 spaces, as free [3][6]. Cars with an electric-vehicle plate may park free for up to 2.5 hours while charging at a public post, an exemption that ends on 31 December 2026 and excludes the town-hall garage [1]. Phone payment has been available since 1 February 2021 on about 400 managed spaces [9].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The questions are about the station and the centre. A traffic development plan presented on 10 December 2024 gave consultant recommendations, not decisions: link the Schützenplatz with a new foot and cycle bridge and a shuttle, possibly extend Am Walle with a parking deck, optimise the Wallgraben garage and pave the P+R and connect it to the centre [14]. A 2019 council proposal listed as goals to be studied a P+R parking garage west of the station, a garage at the new town hall, a new car park at the castle site and renovating or rebuilding the Wallgraben deck [12]. The Region Hannover's draft transport plan of 2020 rated expanding the P+R at the main station as high priority, which is a draft and not a decision [13]. The underground garage below the new town hall was announced to open to the public on 16 September 2024, with 54 public spaces and 6 for electric vehicles, free at first with a one-hour limit and paid management planned for later [8]. E.ON opened a fast-charging park in May 2026 at Rudolf-Diesel-Ring with twelve charging points of up to 400 kW, according to a trade report [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The city's parking page lists 10 numbered car parks of 18 to 110 spaces, among them Am Walle with 70, the town-hall garage with 80, the privately run, paid Neustadttor garage with 110, and the Am Wallgraben garage with 270, which belongs to Wirtschaftsbetriebe Neustadt [6]. That company, wholly owned by the city, operates parking facilities among other activities, and its report shows a parking result of 56,578 euros for 2024 and 10,326 euros for 2023 [17]. Before the town-hall works the Wallgraben garage usually had well over 80 free spaces on normal working days, according to a city statement of October 2021 [10]. Deutsche Bahn lists three open P+R entries at An der Eisenbahn, with 73, 55 and 75 spaces, open round the clock, without saying whether they are separate lots or giving a tariff [11].

Our data cover the P+R at Neustadt am Rübenberge, with 177 spaces, for about 27 days since late September 2026, whose capacity differs from Deutsche Bahn's figures, so the percentages are approximate. Occupancy averaged about 34% on both weekdays and weekends, with a peak of 74% late on a Wednesday morning. The centre's car parks are not in our data.
